content.thinking:
I'm writing a helper function that generates a gem-like shape by lathing a profile curve into a faceted 3D geometry.

Building the crystal prism geometry, matrix composition for placing gems with orientation and scale, and a merge helper that combines multiple geometries into one buffer. Then I'm defining an arch-curve function to shape the chest lid's rounded profile using sampled points along a half-ellipse.

Now I'm working out the lid extrusion and end-plate dimensions—setting thickness, overhang, and arch offsets so the plates fit snugly around the lid's curved profile and attach via a joint to the chest body.

The hinge joint for the lid uses a forward direction along local z, and I'm confirming the pose rotation sign: rotating -105° about the chest's local x-axis should swing the lid upward and back correctly, since the axis vector aligns with world orientation at build time. I'm checking build order so only the lid gets posed while everything else stays in its original placement, then moving on to finish paint details like the wood grain on the chest.

Now I'm working through the lid's underside lining logic, using a normal threshold to distinguish the interior wall faces from the outer arch surface, and confirming this flag gets set before the pose is applied so it stays correct afterward. For the decorative bands sweeping across the lid, I'm building a smoothed polyline path through local points and sweeping a tapered box-section profile along it with linear interpolation between two radii. Then I shift attention to placing a sack prop, checking its ground height against a nearby mound's footprint since the position might fall just outside the mound's radius, meaning I need to sample the base ground height instead.

For the coin spill spilling out of the sack's mouth, I'm tilting the sack's pitch and yaw slightly so the opening faces upward and outward, then computing the mouth's world position to start a trail of coins scattering downhill along that facing direction for a short distance. With all the pieces worked out, I'm ready to assemble the complete code in one pass.
